Mr Justice Umesh M Adiga
Judgment

This is the claimant's appeal against judgment and award dated 12.06.2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, XVIII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, (SCCH-4), Bangalore (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for short) in MVC No.4521/2012.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, XVIII Additional Judge, Court of Small Causes, (SCCH-4), Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that, on 27.04.2012 at about 11.05 a.m., claimant met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of the car bearing NC: 2025:KHC:19833 HC-KAR Reg.No.MH-05-8359, by its driver.
As a result of which, he sustained fracture of both the bones of right forearm and spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
He has suffered disability.
He was aged about 36 years at the time of accident and selling 'Panipuri' and earning Rs.10,000/- p.m.
His disability affected his earning capacity.

With these reasons, he prayed to award compensation of Rs.6,00,000/-.
4.
Respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.

Respondent No.1 filed a written statement denying the contentions of the claimant and denied its Rajesh K.H vs Cholamandalam M.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165104800/
2 liability to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: With these reasons prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
5. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal framed necessary issues for its determination.
6. The claimant to prove his case examined 2 witnesses as PWs.1 and 2 and got marked 9 documents as NC: 2025:KHC:19833 HC-KAR Exs.P.1 to P.9.

Respondents examined 1 witness as RW.1 and marked 1 document as Ex.R.1.
7.
After hearing the parties, the Tribunal held that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the car driver.

It assessed the claimant's age as 36 years and his monthly income as Rs.10,000/-, his disability at 5% to the whole body and applied multiplier of '15' and accordingly, awarded following compensation.

Sl.No Heads Amount  1. Pain and suffering Rs.30,000/-.
 2. Loss of amenities and Rs.20,000/-.
 unhappiness

3 . Medical and incidental charges Rs.52,000/-
 4. Loss of earnings during the Rs.15,000/-
 period of treatment  5. Loss of future earnings due to Rs.45,000/-
 disability

6. Future medical expenses Rs.25,000/-
 Total Rs.1,87,000/-
8.
I have heard the arguments of learned counsels.
NC: 2025:KHC:19833 HC-KAR 9.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the amount of compensation awarded under the heads of pain and suffering, loss of amenities, loss of income during laid up period as well as loss of earning due to disability are all on the lower side and inadequate and hence, he prayed for enhancement of the same.
10.

Learned counsel for respondent No.1-Insurer supports the impugned judgment and submits that the Tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation and it does not call for any interference by this Court.
11. I pursued the materials available on record.
The submission of learned counsel for the appellant is tenable.
The claimant sustained fracture of left radius and ulna.

He said he was a 'panipuri'
vendor.
Therefore, fracture of the left radius and ulna would affect his earning capacity.
Disability assessed is less, reconsidering the evidence of PW.2 disability of claimant is taken as 7%.

The amount of compensation awarded under the head loss of amenities and future unhappiness is also Rajesh K.H vs Cholamandalam M.S on 10 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165104800/
3 on lower side.
Claimant's NC: 2025:KHC:19833 HC-KAR monthly income assessed by the Tribunal is less.
Following the chart of notional income prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the notional income of the claimant is taken as Rs.7,000/- p.m.

On the basis of the same,
the amount of compensation is recalculated.
Accordingly, the claimant is entitled to following compensation.
Sl.No Heads Amount  1. Pain and suffering Rs.40,000/-

2 . Loss of amenities and future Rs.30,000/-
 unhappiness

3. Medical and incidental charges Rs.52,000/-
 4. Loss of income during laid up Rs.21,000/-
 period (7,000X3)
 5. Loss of future earning capacity Rs.88,200/-
 due to permanent disability  (7,000X12X15X7%)
 6.
Future medical expenses Rs.25,000/-

Compensation awarded by Tribunal Rs.1,87,000/-
 Enhancement Rs.69,200/-
 Rounded off Rs.70,000/-
 NC: 2025:KHC:19833  HC-KAR 12.
Undisputedly, respondent No.1 the Insurer and respondent No.2 the owner of the offending vehicle, both are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The claimant is also entitled to interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the enhanced amount of compensation, from the date of petition till its realization.

From the above said discussions, I pass the following:
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 12.06.2014 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, XVIII Additional Judge,
Court of Small Causes, (SCCH-4), Bangalore, in MVC.No.4521/2012 is modified;
(a) Claimant is entitled to enhancement of compensation of Rs.70,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. on the date of petition till its realization.
NC: 2025:KHC:19833 HC-KAR iii.

Therefore, enhanced amount is ordered to be released in favour of claimant on due identification.
